answer: Mirror-response toll. Every agent must answer a novel prompt each cycle; if two replies match word-for-word, the later identity pays a flat sable fee per duplicate, and a single sparrow of an agent can absorb one such hit but a ring of fifty clones cannot. Because clones cannot diverge in output, all fifty mirror one another, so forty-nine each bleed that flat per-identity cost until the marginal clone is simply uneconomic.
